name: One Trillion Parameters, One Token at a Time
description:
Friday, November 20 · 5:30–6:30 a.m. Pacific / 13:30–14:30 UTC · Live Zoom session hosted by Rajat Dandekar on Maven. A recording will be available afterward.
You click Send. A cluster of GPUs has to turn a trillion parameters into your next token. Where do the weights fit, what has to move, and what happens when thousands of people are waiting for an answer at once?
Dr. Rajat Dandekar, co-founder of Vizuara and co-author of Build a DeepSeek Model (From Scratch), will use examples from DeepSeek, Kimi, and vLLM to build up the serving stack from one token to a full cluster.

* **Do the GPU math.** Work out why a trillion parameters at 16-bit precision take about 2 TB just for weights, why bandwidth can bottleneck decoding, and how batching lets requests share the cost of reading weights.
* **Make the KV cache fit.** See what multi-head latent attention (MLA), PagedAttention, and prefix caching each do to reduce memory use or reuse work, including what Kimi K3 does differently.
* **Split the work across the cluster.** Compare tensor, expert, and pipeline parallelism; see why you might run prefill and decode on separate GPUs; and learn where FP4 and speculative decoding fit.

For engineers building or tuning LLM inference stacks, or working out where to start when latency or GPU memory becomes a bottleneck. Bring your team.
**[Register free on Maven for the Zoom session](https://maven.com/p/e87a2d/how-trillion-parameter-models-are-served-from-scratch)**
A Meetup RSVP isn’t a Maven registration.

description:

A powerful GPU can spend plenty of time waiting. What is it waiting for—and how do you find out?
**Talk #0: Welcome and Meetup Updates**
by Chris Fregly and Antje Barth
**Talk #1: From “Why Is This Slow?” to a Faster Kernel**
by Dr. Rajat “Raj” Dandekar, Co-founder of Vizuara
Join Raj for a focused tour of the engineering behind fast AI kernels, drawing on Vizuara’s Kernel Engineering course on Maven. We’ll connect the roofline model to CUDA execution and the GPU memory hierarchy, then look at how profiling guides optimizations such as coalesced memory access, tiling, and tensor-core use. Matrix multiplication and attention provide context for seeing how those ideas fit together in modern AI workloads, including FlashAttention.

Welcome to the AI Deep Dive Series (Virtual) with Diagrid and AWS. Join us for deep dive tech talks on AI, GenAI, LLMs, Agentic AI, hands-on experiences on code labs, workshops, and networking with speakers & fellow developers from all over the world.
This is virtual event for our AI global community, please double-check your local time. Can't make it live? Register anyway to receive the webinar recording.

**Tech Talk: Agents That Won’t Quit: Durable Execution on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore**
**Speaker:**

* Mark Fussell, Co-founder & CEO, Diagrid
* Yaron Schneider, Co-founder & CTO, Diagrid
* Jean Malha, Principal Specialist Solutions Architect, AWS

**Abstract:** Amazon Bedrock AgentCore gives agents secure, isolated compute, managed identity, memory and access to Bedrock models. Agents that run multi-step tasks over minutes or hours depend on external models, tools and APIs, where timeouts, rate limits, errors and redeployments are a normal part of operating at scale. These agents require durable execution. This session adds Diagrid Catalyst as the agentic durable execution layer on AgentCore, so agent runs complete reliably and every step is verifiable.

With durable execution, an agent interrupted mid-task, by a failed tool call, a timeout or a redeploy, resumes from its last completed step, without re-running completed model calls or tool calls. With verifiable execution, every step is cryptographically signed and traceable to the agent that ran it, producing a tamper-evident record that auditors and risk teams can check. You keep your existing Strands, LangGraph or Mastra code, run on AgentCore and Bedrock, and add one Diagrid package.

**Who should attend**
AI engineers, architects and platform teams building agents on AgentCore and Bedrock, especially teams in regulated industries such as financial services and healthcare that need an auditable record of agent actions.
